segments.text: Today we look at how savings grow when interest is left in the account.
With simple interest you earn the same amount every period, because interest is paid only on the original deposit.
With compound interest, the interest you earned is added to the balance, and next period it earns interest too.
So compounding means interest on interest, and the gap over simple interest widens the longer you wait.
The second idea is frequency: a bank can add interest once a year, once a month or even every day.
More frequent compounding gives a slightly higher effective annual rate, which is why lenders quote an APR and savers should compare effective rates.
